mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% coincident with a monthly drop in HOUST signals weakening consumer and housing demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly decline > 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in INDPRO above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO expansion is not followed by a statistically significant positive 20-day S&P 500 return (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.0% combined with a concurrent rise in PAYEMS signals a tight labor market with wage growth, which pressures corporate margins and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% during a period of negative GDP growth (GDPC1 YoY < 0%) signals aggressive easing, which lowers risk-free rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in RSAFS above 5% signals a surge in consumer savings, which typically precedes a reduction in discretionary spending and weaker retail sales, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in UNRATE below 3.5% alongside a simultaneous drop in PAYEMS signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for two consecutive months signals a manufacturing contraction, which depresses earnings and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
